task_retrieval_key:
An 83-year-old Caucasian male, farmer, presented with sudden onset pain and redness in his right eye. He had no history of ocular trauma or previous ocular surgery, and no relevant family history or ophthalmological conditions. He was not on any topical or systemic medication. The patient had been known to the clinic for 3 months with a hypermature cataract in the right eye and a mature cataract in the left eye. He was scheduled for cataract extraction in the left eye first, followed by the right eye. During the preoperative consultation for the left eye cataract surgery, he reported acute ocular pain and photophobia in the right eye that began a few days prior. Clinical examination showed visual acuity of light perception in the right eye and counting fingers in the left eye. Intraocular pressure was 50 mmHg in the right eye and 13 mmHg in the left eye. Slit lamp biomicroscopy of the right eye revealed circumciliary congestion, diffuse corneal edema, pseudohypopyon, complete lens opacification, and suspended white particles in the anterior chamber and pupillary area.
